title: My Family Sold Me for $7 Million. I Owned Their Building
synopsis: Branded a curse at birth, Avery is sold for $7 million to replace her sister in a marriage deal. Her family thinks she is worthless, unaware she secretly owns their mansion, rescue loans, and key Manhattan properties. After signing a clean-break agreement, Avery lets their greed destroy them through fraud, bankruptcy, and arrests. The rejected daughter rises as one of New York’s toughest landlords while everyone who tried to sell her loses everything.
intro: Avery was branded a curse at birth, and her family sells her to replace her sister in a marriage deal, sure she is worthless. It reads like a revenge novel, now on screen: the daughter they rejected secretly owns their mansion, their rescue loans and key Manhattan properties. After a clean-break agreement, she simply lets their greed do the rest, and the people who tried to sell her lose everything.
why: A family-revenge story where the heroine wins by stepping back, not by shouting.
The rejected daughter turns out to hold every card, which makes each scene a slow reveal.
Good pick if you like rags-to-power stories set in New York real estate.

faq.q: Is My Family Sold Me for $7 Million. I Owned Their Building worth watching?
faq.a: If you enjoy family revenge and a heroine who is quietly a step ahead, yes. It is about the fall of the family that underestimated her.
Avery, the daughter her family branded a curse, and the family who sells her into a marriage deal in place of her sister.
